2024.explanation: SAP announced a restructuring plan driven by a strategic shift toward AI, intending to realign its workforce to focus on AI-driven business transformation while allowing overall headcount to remain roughly flat by year end through redeployment and new hiring in AI-related roles.

Intuit eliminated roles to shift resources toward AI-powered products, replacing departing employees with new hires specifically focused on artificial intelligence — the company planned to hire at least as many workers as it cut in fiscal 2025 to accelerate AI integration across its offerings, including the AI-powered financial assistant Intuit Assist and AI-enhanced versions of TurboTax and QuickBooks.

The layoffs were part of Grammarly's business restructuring to advance its focus on 'the AI-enabled workplace of the future,' signaling a strategic realignment around AI that rendered existing roles redundant.

Dell reorganized its go-to-market teams around a new group focused on artificial intelligence services, shifting investment priorities in ways that eliminated sales and marketing roles. Internally, leadership stated, "We are getting leaner. We're streamlining layers of management and reprioritizing where we invest," as the company restructured to absorb the growing AI server business while offsetting margin pressure caused by rising AI infrastructure demand.

2025.explanation: Amazon made cuts to streamline operations and reduce bureaucracy while redirecting resources toward generative AI investment, as the company said it was cutting roles "in order to help make the company leaner and less bureaucratic, while it looks to invest in generative AI."

Salesforce's Agentforce AI agents automated customer support tasks to the point where CEO Marc Benioff directly attributed the elimination of 4,000 support roles to the technology, stating "I've reduced it from 9,000 heads to about 5,000, because I need less heads" and crediting "the benefits and efficiencies of Agentforce" for handling roughly 50% of the customer division's workload, rendering thousands of human support positions redundant.

HP explicitly stated it will cut 4,000 to 6,000 employees through fiscal 2028 by deploying more AI tools, targeting $1 billion in annualized gross run rate savings. The reductions were identified as affecting teams in product development, internal operations, and customer support, as AI is adopted to speed up product development and improve customer satisfaction.

Workday cut 1,750 jobs as part of a strategic shift to invest heavily in artificial intelligence, redirecting resources and headcount toward AI development and deployment across its enterprise software platform.

OpenText cut the 1,600 jobs after CEO Mark Barrenechea issued a 10-point AI mandate to employees, telling staff that embracing AI was a "number one priority and baseline expectation" — signaling that roles unable to align with the company's AI-first direction were eliminated as part of that strategic shift.

Autodesk restructured its workforce to realign resources around AI-driven product development and a shift toward automated, self-service sales and direct billing models, which reduced the need for traditional sales and support roles. The CEO indicated the company was repositioning to capitalize on this operational transition, which was accelerated by investments in AI tooling across its design and engineering software platform.

Recruit Holdings shifted strategic investment heavily toward artificial intelligence, with CEO Hisayuki 'Deko' Idekoba telling employees 'we must adapt' to AI as the driving rationale for the cuts, which targeted R&D and operations teams across both platforms amid a broader consolidation of Indeed and Glassdoor's operations under an AI-first model.

Salesforce eliminated over 1,000 roles as part of a deliberate workforce restructuring to shift resources toward its agentic AI platform, Agentforce, simultaneously announcing plans to hire 2,000 new employees focused on selling AI products. The cuts reflected a strategic pivot away from traditional roles toward positions requiring deeper expertise in automation and AI, repositioning Salesforce as an AI- and data-led company.
Zomato automated its customer service operations using its AI platform 'Nugget,' directly displacing the 600 customer support associates whose roles were rendered redundant by the technology.

CEO George Kurtz stated that advances in artificial intelligence were central to the restructuring, with CrowdStrike's use of AI technology described as something that "flattens our hiring curve," reducing the need for headcount growth. Kurtz cited AI efficiencies as a key driver behind eliminating the 500 positions, framing AI as a force "reshaping every industry" and enabling the company to streamline operations without proportional staffing increases.

Paycom laid off hundreds of workers as the company automated roles using its own AI-powered HR and payroll technology, with internal AI tools taking over tasks previously performed by human employees across its workforce operations.

The layoffs were driven by Just Eat Takeaway's integration of automation and artificial intelligence into its operations, with the company cutting roles as it restructured its cost base partly by automating functions previously performed by employees.

Students abandoned Chegg's paid homework-help platform in favor of free AI tools like ChatGPT, causing revenue to plummet and forcing the company to restructure amid what it called the 'new realities' of artificial intelligence, compounded by a sharp decline in traffic from Google search that had historically driven users to its platform.

VerSe Innovation eliminated approximately 350 roles as part of a broader restructuring to boost profitability and accelerate its push into artificial intelligence, realigning operations with long-term AI-driven business priorities.

TomTom embraced artificial intelligence and adopted a scalable, product-led framework for developing and delivering products, which rendered certain roles in its application layer, sales, and support functions redundant. CEO Harold Goddijn stated that "with a modernized technology stack, we are becoming a truly product-led company, providing our customers with integration-friendly, easily customizable, modular products," with the organizational realignment directly resulting in the elimination of 300 roles.

Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff explicitly credited AI as enabling the company to reduce its workforce, stating that artificial intelligence had let him slash support staff and describing it as an 'exciting' labor replacement, directly linking the cuts to the company's accelerating push into AI-driven automation of roles previously held by human workers.

Fiverr's CEO and founder Micha Kaufman declared the company was pivoting to an "AI-first" business strategy, describing the restructuring as a "painful reset" that eliminated roles across the organization as AI capabilities took over functions previously performed by staff.

Students increasingly turned to AI-powered tools such as ChatGPT over traditional edtech platforms, directly eroding Chegg's user base and revenue and forcing the company to cut costs and streamline operations. The shift represented a structural market disruption in which AI-driven alternatives rendered Chegg's core homework-help business model obsolete, contributing to a loss of roughly $14 billion in market value over three years.

Broadcom cut sales and account management roles as it pivoted its business strategy to capitalize on the AI boom, shifting resources and focus toward AI-driven chip demand rather than maintaining its traditional sales infrastructure.

The laid-off staff at King.com were set to be replaced by the very AI tools they had helped build, with sources indicating that the roles eliminated were directly automated by internal AI systems developed during those employees' tenure at the company.

Yotpo restructured around an AI-led strategy, shutting down its Email and SMS marketing operations and refocusing on core products — Reviews and Loyalty — as the e-commerce sector shifted toward AI-driven solutions. The pivot involved divesting non-core business lines and reorienting the company's platform around AI capabilities, directly eliminating the roles tied to the discontinued product areas.

The 200 European customer service roles were eliminated as part of a restructuring effort to strengthen customer service through smarter routing and AI-powered tools, with Atlassian having already integrated AI into features such as customer contact forms. This followed an earlier round in which 150 customer service employees were cut, with some of those roles also explicitly attributed to AI replacement.

Jamf cut 166 roles as part of a strategic reinvestment plan explicitly tied to boosting spending on artificial intelligence, redirecting resources away from go-to-market and sales functions toward AI development to drive long-term growth and improve operating margins.

Atlassian eliminated 150 customer support and operations roles, replacing them with AI automation to increase efficiency and reduce costs, as part of a broader restructuring of its customer support function that included rolling out AI-embedded customer contact solutions.

Bird restructured its global operations as part of a strategic realignment driven by its pivot toward AI-powered business communication tools, shifting resources away from legacy roles that AI-driven automation rendered redundant.

Palantir reduced its internal IT team from over 200 to fewer than 80 full-time employees as part of a broader strategy to decentralize technology operations, with the company leaning on AI tooling and large language models to maintain operational efficiency with a dramatically smaller headcount. CEO Alex Karp has stated the company will "grow 10x … with fewer employees than we have today," reflecting a deliberate model in which AI capabilities replace traditional internal support roles.

AppsFlyer's CEO Oren Kaniel stated the company would focus on AI and scalability as part of its long-term growth plans, driving a strategic restructuring that eliminated roles no longer aligned with that AI-centered direction.

Google accelerated layoffs to redirect spending toward artificial intelligence infrastructure, cutting roles as part of a broader shift in resource allocation prioritizing AI investment over existing headcount.

CEO Garrett Lord declared a 'refounding' of Handshake centered entirely on its fast-growing AI business, which scaled from zero to $100M in annualized revenue in eight months, and announced he was going 'all in' in re-orienting Handshake's entire business around its AI prospects — cutting roles primarily from the legacy recruiting business vertical to fund a leaner, faster push into AI-driven hiring and post-training data services for frontier labs.

Yellow.ai's shift from conversational AI to autonomous agentic AI directly drove the cuts, with the company stating that this technology transition "changed both how its customers use the product and how the startup builds and supports it, requiring fewer people to build, implement and support it." The layoffs predominantly hit engineering and product teams as automation reduced the headcount needed to develop, deploy, and maintain its platform.

Salesforce has been restructuring its workforce to realign resources toward AI development, having publicly committed to aggressive investment in agentic AI products while reducing headcount in roles made redundant by automation and AI-driven efficiency gains.

Klue cut 40 percent of its workforce to reposition itself for an AI-driven market in which its customers were increasingly experimenting with AI tools internally rather than paying for Klue's competitive intelligence platform, creating direct pricing and demand uncertainty. CEO Jason Smith captured the core challenge: "There is ambiguity about what people will pay for."

Lightricks reorganized its entire workforce structure around its newly unveiled AI video generation model, which enables users to create videos from text prompts and is positioned as a cheaper alternative to OpenAI's Sora, making numerous existing roles redundant while the company simultaneously expanded its AI team.

BenchSci cut 23 percent of its staff as it went all-in on adopting generative AI to perform work formerly done by humans, citing productivity gains from AI while claiming it was not facing any business challenges. The company stated the decision stemmed from 'shifts in the economic environment, operational efficiencies, and adaptation to technological advancements, specifically Generative AI,' and the CEO instituted a policy of asking 'Could AI do this?' before adding any new people or processes.

Deepwatch's CEO stated the layoffs allow the company to accelerate investments in "AI and automation," signaling a deliberate restructuring to redirect resources toward automated cybersecurity capabilities.

Unbabel, a machine translation and AI-powered localization company, carried out the restructuring to adapt to shifts in the broader language services market driven by rapid advancements in AI, which has commoditized automated translation and reduced demand for human-assisted workflows that underpinned its business model.

Culture Amp cut 60 jobs as part of a strategic realignment shifting focus toward new AI-powered products, including the launch of its personalized coaching tool AI Coach, redirecting resources away from existing roles to support its AI product development.

Whatfix's layoffs were triggered by increased adoption of AI within the company, with the company restructuring its workforce as part of a broader shift toward AI-driven operations and growth. Artificial intelligence was cited as one of the direct factors behind the decision to cut roles across the organization.
Google eliminated 50 roles as part of a broader restructuring driven by its prioritization of artificial intelligence investments and the resulting streamlining of its workforce.

Altruist's CEO Jason Wenk acknowledged the company is "all in on AI" and that AI adoption enables it to "get a lot more done with less people," directly reducing headcount needs as the firm competes against Schwab and Fidelity. Wenk stated that AI's primary impact is on "how many customers we can serve without having to have a huge team," with the company deploying AI across finance, compliance, recruiting, and engineering, and having launched its AI-powered advisor assistant Hazel earlier in 2025.

Aurora Labs pivoted away from its original automotive software focus to concentrate on AI-driven high-performance computing (HPC) monitoring for vehicles and data centers, a strategic shift that rendered a large portion of its existing workforce redundant and necessitated the restructuring.

Salesforce cut roles in Ireland as part of its broader workforce restructuring driven by AI automation, as the company has been actively replacing traditional sales and support functions with AI-powered agents, reducing headcount in favor of its own Agentforce platform.

AI's transformation of how games are built, shared, and played restructured the competitive landscape for interactive media platforms, forcing Ludeo to reorganize its workforce as the technology rendered portions of its existing operational model obsolete.

VSCO restructured to operate as an AI-native company, shifting focus away from its declining consumer business toward building tools for professional photographers. The transition to an AI-native model drove the elimination of roles across marketing, technology, and program management.

Verbit's core business of human-assisted transcription has been directly disrupted by AI-powered automated transcription tools, which have commoditized services the company built its $600M valuation on, forcing repeated workforce reductions as AI automation displaces the human labor model underlying its operations.

Textio restructured its workforce to invest in a 'different mix of roles,' a shift driven by the rapid advancement of AI-powered writing tools that disrupted the augmented writing market the company had been built around. As generative AI commoditized core writing assistance capabilities, Textio realigned its team composition to remain competitive in an AI-transformed landscape.

Canva cut roles directly as a result of AI-driven changes to its workforce, with the layoffs explicitly described as AI-related and affecting employees whose functions were increasingly being handled by automated tools and AI-powered features within the platform.
Boozt cut 10% of its permanent workforce as the company planned to compensate for the reduced headcount through greater use of AI tools, effectively replacing those roles with AI-driven automation.

Google cut jobs across multiple units to redirect investment toward artificial intelligence, as the company restructured its workforce to prioritize AI development over maintaining existing headcount in non-AI functions.

Amazon cut thousands of corporate roles as it spends heavily on AI, with the company explicitly framing the reductions as preparation for "wide adoption of AI technology" and under investor pressure to tighten finances amid the AI race. The restructuring targeted layers of corporate management alongside AI, analytics, and marketing divisions, with Amazon aiming to "reduce layers" as automation and AI investment reshaped its workforce needs.

WiseTech Global cut roles as part of a workforce review focused on "maximizing efficiency via automation and use of artificial intelligence," undertaking a two-year restructuring built around AI that is expected to eliminate approximately 2,000 jobs, or roughly a third of its global workforce.

Amdocs created a new GenAI & Data division dedicated to implementing AI company-wide, with the explicit goal of making artificial intelligence "an integral part of DNA" — a structural reorganization that directly drove the layoffs, marking what the company acknowledged as a turning point from routine workforce trimming to AI-led transformation.
Klaviyo restructured its R&D organization with an explicit emphasis on AI and technical skills, eliminating roles that no longer aligned with that strategic direction.

Verily eliminated its entire medical devices program as Alphabet shifted more resources to AI and data infrastructure, with the CEO's memo stating that given Verily's evolving "data and AI strategy, we cannot support the investment of the resources necessary for the long-term growth and scaling of our Devices programs."

2026.explanation: Oracle attributed the layoffs directly to AI adoption across its operations, stating that "the adoption and deployment of AI technologies across our operations have resulted, and may continue to result, in reductions to our workforce."

The layoffs were framed as a continuation of organizational restructuring to reduce management layers and bureaucracy, with Beth Galetti noting the cuts were part of work to strengthen the organization by "reducing layers, increasing ownership, and removing bureaucracy" — a restructuring effort widely understood to be accelerated by Amazon's shift toward AI-driven automation reducing the need for middle management and operational roles.

Dell limited external hiring and restructured operations to reduce costs while shifting its business model toward AI infrastructure, with the company describing the cuts as part of "disciplined cost management" as it transforms from a hardware company into an AI server provider.

The layoffs were driven by Meta's aggressive pivot toward AI investment, with the company restructuring its workforce to redirect resources into AI development and infrastructure, eliminating roles deemed redundant in an AI-driven operational model.

Block eliminated roughly half its workforce as part of a sweeping restructuring driven by the company's push to automate work through AI, reducing its reliance on large employee headcounts across operations and product functions.

Cisco's CEO Chuck Robbins framed the cuts as a strategic reallocation toward AI-era competitiveness, stating that "the companies that will win in the AI era will be those with focus, urgency, and the discipline to continuously shift investment toward the areas where demand and long-term value creation are strongest." While reducing headcount in some areas, Cisco simultaneously announced targeted investments in silicon, optics, security, and employee use of AI across the company.

Intuit restructured its workforce to redirect resources toward AI development, with CEO Sasan Goodarzi framing the cuts as necessary to accelerate the company's AI push, including bets on partnerships with Anthropic and OpenAI to transform products like TurboTax, QuickBooks, Credit Karma, and Mailchimp. The layoffs were driven by a strategic decision to streamline operations and reduce organizational complexity in order to fund and prioritize AI integration across its core product lines.

WiseTech conducted a two-year restructuring explicitly built around AI, with CEO Zubin Appoo stating that "artificial intelligence-fueled savings will ultimately cut through the entire company" — meaning AI-driven automation was expected to replace roles across all functions, not just in software development. The company described the overhaul as a "deep AI transformation," directly tying the elimination of nearly a third of its global workforce to the integration of AI into both its customer-facing software and internal operations.

Atlassian cut 1,600 employees to self-fund further investment in artificial intelligence and enterprise sales, executing a strategic pivot toward AI capabilities that required restructuring its workforce and redirecting resources away from existing roles.

Reality Labs' budget was slashed by 30% to redirect funds toward superintelligence research, with the 1,500 affected employees cut as Meta pivoted resources away from VR development and into AI infrastructure and capabilities.

Cloudflare eliminated approximately 1,100 roles as part of a strategic shift toward AI-driven infrastructure and automation, reallocating resources to accelerate its AI and networking product expansion in a rapidly restructuring cloud and security market.

Autodesk shed roughly 1,000 jobs to redirect spending toward its cloud platform and artificial intelligence efforts, with the cuts described as the final phase of a multi-year restructuring tied to its cloud and AI strategy. The elimination of primarily customer-facing sales roles reflected a deliberate reallocation of investment away from traditional go-to-market functions and toward AI and cloud infrastructure.

Livspace executed a phased internal reorganisation aimed at transforming the company into an AI-native organisation, shifting to AI-driven operations to lower costs and enhance AI integration across its business. The restructuring, which also saw co-founder Saurabh Jain exit, reflected a strategic pivot away from traditional workforce-dependent operations toward automated, AI-led processes.

Ocado cut 1,000 jobs as part of a £150 million cost-saving drive, with the restructuring tied to the company's shift toward automating its warehouse and logistics operations through its proprietary robotics and AI-powered fulfillment technology, reducing the need for human roles as those systems scaled.

Snap cited AI-driven efficiencies as the direct cause of the restructuring, reducing its global workforce as the company shifted resources toward AI-powered tools and automation that replaced functions previously handled by human employees.

Wix cut its workforce as part of a restructuring plan driven by the fast evolution of AI, which made many roles increasingly redundant in the AI era, while also pressuring the company's profitability through rising AI-related costs.

UKG cited AI-driven changes as the reason for the restructuring, with the company explicitly framing the cuts as part of a global transformation tied to AI investment and a strategic shift toward frontline workforce products, where automation is reshaping the human capital management software landscape.

LinkedIn restructured to concentrate resources on higher-impact priorities and long-term growth, with CEO Daniel Shapero realigning engineering, product, marketing, and global business teams as Microsoft-owned platforms accelerated investment in AI-driven features that reduced the need for headcount in those functions.

Pinterest cut roughly 700 roles as part of a strategic shift to invest heavily in AI-driven product development, redirecting resources away from existing headcount toward building and scaling AI-powered features across its platform.

Meta cut these 700 positions as part of a broad pivot away from its metaverse strategy and toward artificial intelligence, with Reality Labs' budget slashed as the company redirected investment into AI priorities. The layoffs, described internally as "right-sizing" its investment in Reality Labs, reflected a structural decision to wind down metaverse-era headcount and reallocate resources to AI-driven initiatives across the business.

CEO Brian Armstrong restructured Coinbase around an 'AI-native' operating model — capping management at five layers, eliminating pure manager roles, and moving toward 'one person teams' — with AI tools absorbing work previously performed by the eliminated positions. The company explicitly repositioned itself 'for the artificial intelligence era,' with Armstrong citing AI rapidly changing how the company operates as a direct driver of the workforce reduction.

The cuts were made to redirect investment toward Monday.com's AI Work Platform, abandoning the traditional seat-based software model in favor of AI agents that automate tasks and make decisions without human input. The company stated the restructuring was designed to "support a leaner, more focused operating model" as it refocused resources around AI projects.

ZoomInfo restructured as AI fundamentally repriced the B2B sales intelligence market, eroding demand for the data products that formed its core business and forcing a strategic pivot toward AI-focused operations. The company closed its Israel R&D center and cut roles across the U.S., India, and the U.K. as it shifted resources to remain competitive in an AI-driven landscape, targeting $60 million in annual cost savings through the 2026 Restructuring Program.

Freshworks restructured operations because AI had taken over a growing share of internal functions, with CEO Dennis Woodside stating in an internal letter to staff that "over half of our code is written by AI" — directly displacing engineering, QA, sales, and management roles that had previously required human labor.

Groupon eliminated up to 400 positions globally as part of Project Foundry, a strategic initiative to rebuild the company as an AI-native organization, with human roles in corporate functions, operations, and sales replaced by automation and AI-driven operations to generate $20–$25 million in annual savings.

Paytm executed the layoffs as part of a broader workforce restructuring driven by its aggressive pivot toward AI, simultaneously announcing plans to hire approximately 4,000 employees in AI, product, and technology roles over the next nine months, effectively replacing lower-performing headcount with AI-focused talent as the company pursued a leaner, technology-driven operational model.

Lastminute cut approximately 400 roles as part of a strategic pivot toward AI-driven automation in its travel booking and customer service operations, redirecting investment into artificial intelligence tools that replaced functions previously handled by human staff.

Angi's workforce reduction was carried out to optimize organizational structure and reduce operating expenses "in light of AI-driven efficiency improvements," as stated in the company's SEC filing, indicating that AI automation had made a significant portion of existing roles redundant.

Ticketmaster restructured its engineering, product, and design teams as part of an AI-focused strategy, framing AI as a core operational utility and redirecting resources toward AI-driven product development to replace functions previously handled by those roles.

GitLab restructured to position itself for what CEO Bill Staples called "the agentic era," scaling its DevSecOps platform around AI capabilities and agentic workflows, which rendered a significant portion of existing roles redundant. The company simultaneously exited 22 countries and reduced its geographic footprint by 37%, reflecting a broad operational realignment driven by the shift toward AI-native software development.

Innovaccer restructured its workforce as part of a deliberate transition to become an AI-native company, replacing roles across its India and U.S. teams with AI-led operations. The cuts came months after a $275 million funding round, signaling that the capital was being redirected toward AI infrastructure rather than headcount growth.

Rapid7's restructuring was driven by a deliberate pivot to an AI-first platform strategy, with the board-approved plan redirecting investment toward core AI-driven cybersecurity capabilities while eliminating roles tied to operations and functions outside that strategic focus.

TikTok's automated systems had reached the point where they were handling 85% of all content removals for guideline violations, directly undermining the operational case for maintaining large distributed human moderation teams across regional hubs. As AI took over the bulk of content review work, Trust and Safety roles focused on queue management, quality checking, and local content review were eliminated in favor of a smaller number of more specialized positions.

Sprout Social's CEO Ryan Barretto stated that software companies now need to operate and invest differently, signaling a strategic shift driven by AI's transformation of the industry. The company restructured to focus on AI-powered social intelligence, redirecting resources away from roles made redundant by AI-driven automation.

The restructuring was explicitly designed to redirect funds toward Arctic Wolf's Aurora Superintelligence platform and an agentic Security Operations Center (SOC), with the company stating the cuts were necessary to invest more heavily in AI and automated security operations.

DeepL's CEO Jarek Kutylowski framed the cuts as a deliberate structural response to AI-driven transformation, stating: 'We are currently living through a massive structural shift in what work exists, who does it, and how many people it takes to do it well, and that shift is because of AI.' He described a vision of an 'AI native company' where AI is embedded so deeply into operations that 'smaller groups - sometimes even an individual - [can] do work that once required entire teams,' making a larger headcount structurally unnecessary.

Opendoor shut down its entire India operation, eliminating 250 roles that had been dedicated to running the company's manual workflows, as it shifted to greater use of AI. CEO Kaz Nejatian confirmed the move was driven by the transition toward AI, which made the manual, outsourced work in India redundant.

TikTok shifted content moderation work to AI, eliminating the need for the human moderators based in its Nashville office and driving the closure of that facility. The move raised concerns about whether automated systems could handle trust and safety responsibilities with the same fairness as human reviewers.

CEO Tomer Weingarten said the layoffs are intended to improve efficiency and sharpen the company's focus on its more profitable AI and data operations, signaling a strategic shift away from roles not aligned with that trajectory.

SSense eliminated its entire full-time photography, retouching, and hair-and-makeup teams as it accelerated its adoption of AI-generated fashion imagery, replacing traditional content production workflows with AI-powered tools and virtual fashion imaging. These cuts were part of a broader restructuring that included multiple rounds of layoffs across the company.

Envato, acquired by Shutterstock, underwent a major restructuring driven by Shutterstock's broader strategy to consolidate its creative asset platforms and invest heavily in AI-generated content tools, rendering numerous roles in content curation, licensing, and operations redundant as AI automation took over functions previously performed by human staff.

Meta cut 200 roles as part of a broader workforce restructuring driven by its aggressive pivot toward AI, with CEO Mark Zuckerberg having signaled that AI tools would increasingly perform work previously done by software engineers and other staff, reducing headcount needs across technical and operational functions. The Burlingame and Sunnyvale cuts reflected Meta's reallocation of resources toward AI infrastructure and development, replacing human roles with automated systems as the company scaled its AI capabilities.
MRI Software cited AI adoption as the direct reason for the cuts, using automation to streamline operations as its private equity owners positioned the company for a potential $10 billion sale.

Jumia expanded its use of AI automation across cybersecurity processes, code quality workflows, and seller management systems, with the efficiency gains from these deployments directly reducing the need for human headcount across its operations.

Artlist restructured around an AI-native operating model, eliminating roughly 40% of its workforce as AI capabilities absorbed functions previously requiring human headcount, even as the company surpassed $300 million in annual recurring revenue and continued to grow.
Mews's founder Richard Valtr directly attributed the cuts to AI, stating that the technology had made the affected roles redundant as part of the company's deepest restructuring since the pandemic.

Upwork eliminated roles as part of a strategic shift to invest in and integrate AI capabilities into its platform, with the restructuring reflecting a repositioning of the workforce around AI-driven products and services rather than the headcount-intensive functions those roles previously supported.

CEO Jeff Yabuki cited AI productivity gains and a strategic shift to productized innovation as the drivers behind the restructuring, with the cuts concentrated in the Digital Wealth division covering financial planning, advisor experience, and client experience software.

Epidemic Sound pivoted toward AI-driven music generation, automating creative and operational functions that had previously required human staff, prompting the company to shed one-third of its workforce as it restructured around AI tooling rather than human-led production.

Kraken cut staff primarily due to a sharp decline in digital-asset prices driving cost reduction efforts, but the restructuring also reflected broader industry shifts as crypto exchanges accelerated investment in AI-driven automation to handle trading infrastructure and customer operations with fewer human employees, displacing roles that had previously required manual oversight.

Chime cited a strategic shift toward AI-driven automation as the basis for the cuts, with leadership indicating the company was restructuring operations to reduce headcount in roles that could be handled by AI tools, redirecting investment toward AI-powered product development and efficiency improvements.

The layoffs are part of Intuit's broader restructuring of its Credit Karma subsidiary, driven by integration changes and operational consolidation as Intuit redirects investment toward AI-driven product development across its portfolio, eliminating roles made redundant by automation and platform consolidation even as Credit Karma's revenue surged to $631 million.

Former MercadoLibre  employees revealed that they had spent significant portions of their work training the automated systems that ultimately replaced them, reviewing dozens of conversations per week, refining AI responses, and improving the empathy of chatbots now handling customer and seller interactions on platforms including MercadoLibre's WhatsApp channel.

Skai laid off 20% of its workforce as part of an AI-driven transformation, retooling its global operations model in response to the rapid adoption of artificial intelligence across its business functions.

Elementor described the layoffs as an organizational "reset" aimed at preparing for the next generation of website creation in the AI era, reflecting a broader AI-driven restructuring as automation increasingly reshapes how websites are built and what roles are needed to support that process.

The layoffs were carried out as part of a restructuring exercise aimed at accelerating the adoption of artificial intelligence across GoKwik's operations, impacting employees across departments including customer onboarding.

Patreon's CEO Jack Conte cited AI's transformative impact on the tech industry and workplace dynamics as a key driver of the restructuring, framing it as an AI-driven reorganization that included flattening management layers and shifting toward an AI-first strategy.

Pendo's CEO Todd Olson attributed the cuts to rapid adoption of artificial intelligence tools, framing the restructuring as a 'refounding' as tech budgets shift toward AI agents, displacing roles tied to Pendo's traditional product analytics workflows.

Bitgo's workforce reduction was driven by a strategic pivot toward AI-powered infrastructure, with CEO Mike Belshe stating the company needed to "concentrate our people and energy on the areas that matter most: security, trading, stablecoins, settlement, and AI-powered infrastructure," requiring a leaner, more deliberate organizational structure to compete in a dramatically changed financial services landscape.

Salesforce eliminated roles across its Agentforce AI product, MuleSoft, and Marketing Cloud divisions as the company restructured around AI-driven priorities, with concern mounting that AI could replace some of its traditional software services.

Clari's revenue forecasting platform increasingly relies on AI-driven automation to perform functions that previously required dedicated sales operations and analytics roles, reducing headcount needs following its merger with SalesLoft. The consolidation of two AI-powered revenue intelligence platforms created significant role redundancy, as overlapping AI and automation capabilities across both companies eliminated the need for duplicate positions.

Lightricks restructured around AI by separating its profitable Facetune consumer app business from its costly push into AI video generation models under the LTX brand, with the expense of developing frontier video models driving the need to cut headcount for the second time in under six months.

Snowflake eliminated its entire technical writing and documentation team as AI tools took over content generation responsibilities, with the cuts described as moves to 'align our teams with Snowflake's long-term strategy.' The layoffs were widely characterized as one of the most aggressive pivots toward AI-generated content in the enterprise software sector, reflecting a broader AI-driven reorganization under CEO Sridhar Ramaswamy that has eliminated close to 700 positions since he took over.

Culture Amp's repeated rounds of layoffs reflect its strategic pivot toward AI-powered HR products, as the company restructured roles to align with an AI-focused product direction — a shift that had been underway since at least its 2024 layoffs, which were explicitly tied to a focus on AI products.

GeoComply restructured its workforce as part of a broader shift toward AI-driven automation in geolocation compliance and fraud detection, areas where the company had been investing heavily in machine learning tools that reduced the need for manual operational and support roles.

BenchSci cut staff as it shifted its operating model toward AI agents, which automated work previously performed by human employees, directly eliminating the need for those roles. The layoff was explicitly framed as a consequence of embracing AI agents to carry out core functions of the business.

Acko restructured its workforce as part of a deliberate shift toward integrating AI into its operations, with the layoffs attributed to AI-led automation realigning and displacing roles across the organization.

SuperOps restructured its engineering team as part of a deliberate pivot to become an AI-first SaaS organization, with the cuts framed as accelerating its transition into an AI-first company while improving operational efficiency. The layoffs were concentrated in engineering — where AI-driven automation rendered a significant portion of existing roles redundant — as the company repositioned its product and workforce around AI-native capabilities.
Alphabet shut down Verily's medical devices program and redirected resources toward AI, making the roles supporting that program redundant and triggering the workforce reduction.

Multiverse pivoted its business model toward helping corporate clients extract productivity gains from their AI investments, deploying AI-driven upskilling to replace headcount with higher output per employee. A company spokesperson stated: "Companies are looking for ways to create genuine productivity improvements from their AI investments. We're delivering that both for our growing customer base, and at Multiverse, where revenue per employee is up 37%."

ServiceNow eliminated roles as part of a broader restructuring effort driven by its accelerating investment in AI-powered workflow automation, which reduced the need for headcount in functions the platform increasingly handles autonomously. The June 2026 cuts were described as a sweeping reorg — the largest and most shocking tenured employees had seen — reflecting the company's strategic shift toward AI-driven service delivery across IT management and business process automation.

Interview Kickstart underwent a restructuring driven by rising automation due to AI, with cofounder Soham Mehta confirming the workforce reduction was a direct result of that automation push displacing roles across the organization.

VideoAmp cited AI as a "major platform shift" driving the cuts, as the company accelerated its transition toward artificial intelligence and agentic software development, reshaping its core operating model for ad measurement.

One Identity dissolved its longstanding Identity Manager development team in Germany, relocating the work to Hungary where development will continue with the support of AI, making AI-assisted automation central to the restructuring that eliminated the established roles.

Pentera's layoffs were part of a broader strategic shift to allocate more resources to artificial intelligence and innovation, with marketing and headquarters roles cut while engineering and development positions continued to be filled.

LSports cut 40 roles as part of a strategic shift toward AI-driven automation of sports data processing and analytics functions that had previously required human operators, reflecting a broader restructuring of its workforce around automated data pipelines and machine-generated insights.

Shopify's cuts targeted revenue operations and customer support roles — functions the company has been actively automating through AI — and a former staffer cited "technological advancements" as a contributing factor in the eliminations.

Papaya Gaming cited the rapid adoption of artificial intelligence tools as a key driver of the restructuring, stating that AI was changing how teams work and enabling greater operational efficiency, which reduced the need for certain roles.

Foretellix's layoffs followed a period in which wider adoption of AI tools reshaped the company's operational needs, reducing the headcount required to support functions that had previously relied on more staff.

Guesty cut 20 employees as part of a strategic shift toward AI-driven automation of property management workflows, with the company redirecting resources into AI product development to reduce reliance on human-handled operational tasks across its platform.

AI tools devastated Tailwind Labs' business model by enabling developers to generate Tailwind CSS code on demand, collapsing demand for the company's paid templates and UI components and causing an 80% revenue decline and a 40% drop in documentation traffic. CEO Adam Wathan cited the "brutal impact AI has had on our business" as the driving force behind the layoffs, having forecast during the holidays that the company would be unable to meet payroll within six months if nothing changed.

Salesforce restructured its marketing, product, and data teams as part of a broader strategic pivot toward AI-driven products and services, particularly its Agentforce AI platform, which reduced the need for certain traditional roles in those functions. The company had been aggressively reallocating headcount and resources to support AI development and sales, making legacy positions in marketing and data operations redundant.
Firebolt shifted to an AI-first operating model that requires fewer engineers, making a significant portion of its development workforce redundant despite holding over $100 million in cash.

DraftKings restructured its workforce as the company embraced AI-driven automation, reducing headcount to cut general and administrative costs while pivoting capital toward high-growth opportunities, including a $10 billion prediction markets expansion targeting up to $900 million in EBITDA.

Zap Africa explicitly described the cuts as an 'AI-driven efficiency' restructuring, pivoting to a leaner, automation-driven operating model that eliminated roles across its design, operations, marketing, and support teams.

Crypto.com's CEO Kris Marszalek attributed the cuts to an enterprise-wide AI integration, stating the layoffs targeted "roles that do not adapt in our new world" as the company restructured its workforce around AI-driven operations.

Gemini explicitly blamed AI as a factor in the layoffs, with the company shifting strategic focus toward AI-driven operations while simultaneously retreating from international markets. The restructuring reflected a broader repositioning in which AI automation reduced the need for headcount across global teams as the firm consolidated to the U.S. and Singapore.

Monte Caro's CEO Barr Moses cited AI as enabling "smaller, more focused groups to work faster and more effectively," with firsthand evidence of PMs shipping prototypes, support staff resolving issues independently, and SEs shipping customer features — productivity gains that made a larger headcount structurally redundant. The company committed to "rethinking roles from the ground up" using first-principles thinking to "fundamentally transform how every role operates in an AI-first company," eliminating positions not out of financial distress but as a deliberate structural bet that AI-enabled smaller teams could outperform larger ones.

MARA Holdings cut its workforce as part of a deliberate strategic pivot away from Bitcoin mining and toward artificial intelligence infrastructure and high-performance computing, with the staff reductions tied directly to repositioning the company as an AI compute player. The layoffs followed the company's moves into AI and data center operations, including a partnership with Starwood to supervise construction, design, and daily operations of data centers built to support AI workloads.

Bolt's CEO Ryan Breslow announced via Slack that the decision to lay off a third of the company's staff 'became unavoidable,' framing the cuts as part of a strategic pivot toward AI-focused solutions, with the layoffs widely reported as an AI-driven workforce restructuring.

Life360 cut jobs as part of a shift toward greater AI adoption, with CEO Lauren Antonoff acknowledging that "the roles people play are shifting" as the company restructured its workforce around artificial intelligence.

Productboard transformed into what CEO Hubert Palan called an 'AI-only organization' built around its AI product Productboard Spark, eliminating over 30% of its workforce because 'AI is collapsing the process layer of building software,' automating away the mechanics of product development that the company's prior tooling was built to support. Palan framed the restructuring as a deliberate all-at-once shift to 'fewer people, every person at a higher altitude,' replacing a broad team structure with a leaner organization exclusively focused on AI-driven product decision-making.
AI agents were cited as directly replacing human work, prompting 0G Labs to cut a quarter of its workforce as part of a deliberate shift toward AI integration.

reAlpha, an AI-driven real estate technology company, restructured its workforce as part of its strategic pivot toward replacing traditional real estate processes with AI-powered tools, reducing the need for human roles as its core business model centers on automating home buying and related transactions through AI.

AI changed how Bird operates, eliminating roles that previously required dedicated headcount, as founder Robert Vis stated directly: 'The second is AI. It has changed how we work, and tasks that required dedicated headcount even a few years ago no longer do.'

Dune's layoffs were driven by a strategic pivot to concentrate resources on AI-powered data products, with the company going "all-in on two shifts: AI and institutions coming onchain." The launch of Dune MCP, which enables teams and AI agents to build dashboards and workflows without SQL knowledge, allowed the company to automate core data workflows, reducing the headcount needed to support its existing customer base.

Gambling.com launched an AI-driven restructuring program after incoming CEO Kevin McCrystle told analysts that AI now generates about 80% of new engineering code, reducing the need for human headcount in that function. The cuts were expected to save 13 million euros annually as the company moved to make artificial intelligence the core foundation of its operations.

ClickUp's CEO Zeb Evans restructured around what he called a '100x org' model, in which AI agents handle code generation and other workflows, making traditional supporting roles redundant while concentrating output in a smaller number of high-judgment engineers and AI-native operators. Evans stated directly that 'the great engineers, the ones who can orchestrate, architect, and review, are becoming 100x engineers' who direct AI agents rather than write code themselves, rendering the layer of engineers who previously contributed incrementally an 'inherently inefficient bottleneck' — a structural shift that drove the elimination of 22% of headcount.

BigID restructured its workforce as part of a deliberate transition to an 'AI-first' operating model, shifting development priorities toward AI-centric capabilities within its data security and compliance platform. The layoffs reflected the company's move to a more advanced, AI-driven operational structure that reduced the need for headcount under its previous development model.

Webflow's CEO Linda Tong restructured the company around an 'agentic web' AI pivot, repositioning the company's workforce and operations to align with an AI-driven future for web design and development.

Rapyd's CEO Arik Shtilman announced a company-wide restructuring explicitly tied to AI adoption, writing: "Today we are restructuring Rapyd to align with a fundamental shift in our business model: Rapyd is now a company operated by AI." The layoffs followed a strategic decision to reposition the fintech unicorn as an AI-driven organization, with Shtilman describing the goal of building a "unified, AI-driven organization" to scale and grow profitably.

Shopee cut hundreds of developer roles — including quality assurance positions — as part of a broader pivot to AI, joining rivals globally in slashing staff while adopting the technology and building new AI-based services. CEO Forrest Li had declared that a trillion-dollar market capitalisation was achievable if the company doubled down on AI, driving structural shifts that reduced reliance on traditional developer headcount.

Rackspace pivoted sharply away from legacy managed hosting and its Public Cloud unit to redeploy resources toward enterprise AI infrastructure services, with CEO Gajen Kandiah driving the restructuring to position the company as a provider of AI operations and infrastructure rather than traditional managed hosting.

Optimove's CEO Pini Yakuel described the decision to cut 10 percent of staff as "painful," framing it explicitly as a push towards AI, signaling a strategic restructuring of the workforce to prioritize AI-driven operations within the igaming marketing platform.

Snyk restructured its organization to accelerate its transformation into an AI security platform, stating it was "organizing to move at that speed, with a more focused team, a clearer mission, and the tools to build faster," in response to AI and autonomous agents fundamentally changing how software is built and deployed. The company realigned R&D around four focused areas tied to AI-era threats — including AI-written code and autonomous agents in production — simplifying its structure and reducing team sizes to enable faster execution on its Snyk AI Security Platform strategy.

AI-driven transformation of operations changed the shape of how Amperity functioned as a customer data platform, with the workforce reduction aligning with a strategic shift in investment toward automation and AI technology rather than maintaining existing headcount.

Uber cut its customer service workforce as part of what the company described as an "embrace" of AI, directly citing artificial intelligence as the reason for the job cuts and framing the reductions as part of a broader effort to achieve AI-based efficiencies across its operations.

Dutch's cofounder Joe Spector explicitly replaced the entire marketing team with AI-driven tooling that handled A/B testing, brand-lift studies, search strategy, and content production at scale, cutting customer acquisition costs 20% in four months while multiplying content output tenfold at a fraction of the cost of human headcount.

LegalZoom cut staff by 15% in its second round of layoffs in under a year, following the installation of a new CEO, as the company restructured its online legal technology platform amid broader industry automation trends driven by AI-powered legal tools increasingly replacing functions previously handled by human staff.
